diagram_math_checks.result: M=ker(pi)=i(N) by the given short exact sequence. The figure explicitly chooses a homomorphic section as in condition 1; it does not claim an arbitrary extension splits. E=M semidirect_alpha H uses alpha_h(m)=s(h)m s(h)^(-1). Normality of a kernel keeps this in M, conjugation is an automorphism, and homomorphic s gives alpha_h alpha_k=alpha_hk. This is the action in the Statement and step 2.1/L2.

a:M→E sends m to (m,1), p:E→H sends (m,h) to h, j:H→E sends h to (1,h); iota:M→G is inclusion, pi:G→H is the original quotient, and s:H→G is the chosen section. The lower row is exact by M=ker(pi) and surjectivity of pi; the upper row has injective a, surjective p, and ker(p)=a(M). End terms 1 are omitted visually and explicitly restored in prose.

Phi:E→G is (m,h)↦m s(h). With (m,h)(mprime,hprime)=(m alpha_h(mprime),hhprime), Phi of the product equals m s(h) mprime s(hprime), so it is a homomorphism. This is precisely L2 applied to M and K=s(H) from steps 1.1 and 2.1. No centrality, normality of K, or trivial action is assumed.

Psi(g)=(g s(pi(g))^(-1),pi(g)); its first component has quotient pi(g) pi(s(pi(g)))^(-1)=1. Phi(Psi(g))=g. For (m,h), pi(m s(h))=h, so Psi(Phi(m,h))=(m s(h) s(h)^(-1),h)=(m,h). This is the factorisation in step 2.1 together with pi s=id from L1.

Phi(a(m))=m s(1)=m=iota(m), and pi(Phi(m,h))=pi(m) pi(s(h))=h=p(m,h). Also p(j(h))=h, pi(s(h))=h, and Phi(j(h))=s(h). Thus both squares and the section compatibility hold, with arrows j and s directed H→E and H→G. Under Phi the subgroup j(H) becomes s(H)=K, the complement established in steps 1.1 and 2.1; conversely step 3.1 recovers a section from a complement.
